title: Outside money is Plan Z
coreMove: Treat outside capital as Plan Z. First shrink the idea, charge customers earlier, and keep control, then raise only when the model truly cannot start without it.

exampleSpecs.stakes: keep control instead of trading it for a milestone
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the protagonist weighs a venture round against 37signals-style customer-funded growth

exampleSpecs.audience: service founders with an ambitious roadmap
exampleSpecs.stakes: avoid raising to match full scope before testing demand
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the protagonist cuts scope so a customer funds the next step

exampleSpecs.audience: founders one year past a seed round
exampleSpecs.stakes: notice the customer sliding down the priority list
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the protagonist sees post-raise attention reorient toward investors

exampleSpecs.audience: hardware founders facing genuine capital needs
exampleSpecs.stakes: tell a true capital need from a reflex to raise
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the protagonist confirms the model truly requires capital

exampleSpecs.stakes: keep spending discipline after the round lands
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the protagonist catches loosened discipline from unearned cash

exampleSpecs.audience: venture-backed founders near a roadmap fork
exampleSpecs.stakes: choose product quality over a buyer-friendly metric
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the protagonist sees exit thinking compete with product quality
